outcomes.outcome: INPUT and FORWARD drop by default and OUTPUT stays open; a port no rule allows is dropped for any other host
ICMP and SSH are let in from any host
traffic to 127.0.0.0/8 arriving on another interface is rejected (rule 002)

uncovered.why: a packet to 127.0.0.0/8 that arrives on a non-loopback interface never reached INPUT on a lab node, so rule 002 has nothing to act on there
uncovered.lifted_by: capability: a node kind whose kernel passes a 127.0.0.0/8 destination from another interface to INPUT
uncovered.evidence: measured 2026-11-18 on the ubuntu node (firewall_secure_extra's set, the same rule): 3 hand-built frames from the peer to 127.0.0.1 through the node's NIC were counted 0 by rule 002 with route_localnet 0 (the kernel drops that destination before INPUT) and again 0 with route_localnet 1 (escalations/firewall_secure_extra.behaviour.md)

outcomes.outcome: whitelisted hosts (the Hiera list plus the acl) reach SSH without any limit
other hosts are rate-limited against SSH brute force (overall 20 a minute with a burst of 5, 8 held per host, 15 new a minute per host)
rules Puppet does not manage are purged at the next agent run (strict_purge true)
the emergency flush script is installed, clears every rule when run, and the next agent run rebuilds the firewall
the running rules are saved for the next boot
strict mode (only listed hosts reach SSH), and strict_purge false with ignore_patterns (unmanaged rules matching a pattern kept)
